I'm on a bad power network, sharing a single cable with a crew of workers.

My Pc has a UPS. Still, whenever the powerdrill is used, the mouse stutters and the keyboard turns of for about 20 seconds. My screens seems OK but the pc does seem a little tiny bit slower too...

So, what happened here? Would a better (brand/uptime) UPS be a solution? Any other info that helps me understand and/or prevent this?
Sharing power line: PC malfunctions despite UPS. Please, ELI5 what to do to prevent/fix this

Not sure about your exact situation, but a better UPS might be the answer. I don't suppose you have a wireless mouse and/or keyboard do you? If so, it's possible the power drill is causing some interference. Otherwise, the UPS may be at fault. Do the lights flicker when the drill is used?

nope, all wired. All lights flicker, also on the othervoltage controllers on the fridge and such. Well, it's only a couple of weeks more, but the UPS is a chinese brand, so I might consider replacing it with an APC or so. Thanks!

Yep, definitely sounds like a better UPS will help. I've got an APC unit myself. The voltage levels at which the UPS switches to battery power are adjustable on some, and ought to help you out. If you're not too worried about a complete outage, you could go with a lower VA rating and save some money. The higher the VA rating, the longer it will run on battery without needing to be charged.
